title: Animals And Birds Arabic Summary For The 7th Degree Of The 1st Station

questions.question: What do the three truths together lead all kinds of animals to declare?
questions.answer: They all point to the oneness of Allah and testify that only He is worthy of worship.

questions.question: How is the earth described as giving this testimony?
questions.answer: It is pictured like one huge living being speaking this truth in a way that fits its greatness.

questions.question: To whom is the earth’s testimony said to be conveyed?
questions.answer: It is said to be carried to the inhabitants of the heavens.

questions.question: What did the traveler do after seeing this testimony?
questions.answer: He understood it clearly and fully.

questions.question: Which two groups are especially mentioned as being united in this witness?
questions.answer: Animals and birds.

questions.question: In what way are animals and birds described as praising and witnessing?
questions.answer: They do so through their senses, abilities, limbs, and bodily parts.

questions.question: What does it mean that their bodily features are like “words”?
questions.answer: Their well-made parts and abilities show meaningful signs of Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: Which qualities are used to describe the signs found in their senses and powers?
questions.answer: They are balanced, organized, and expressive.

questions.question: Which qualities are used to describe the signs found in their limbs and organs?
questions.answer: They are complete and strong in meaning.

questions.question: What truth about creation is connected to Allah’s will in the passage?
questions.answer: Bringing creatures into existence and making them is tied to His will.

questions.question: What truth about difference and beauty is mentioned?
questions.answer: Their distinct features and decoration are connected to purpose.

questions.question: What truth about measuring and shaping is mentioned?
questions.answer: Their form and proportion are connected to wisdom.

questions.question: From what simple beginnings do these many living forms come?
questions.answer: They come from eggs and drops of sperm that are alike or very similar.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the beginnings and the results?
questions.answer: The beginnings are limited and similar, but the creatures that come from them are countless and varied.

questions.question: What do the endless different forms of animals and birds show about Allah?
questions.answer: They show His power, knowledge, will, purpose, and wisdom.

questions.question: What is the main message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The animal world points together to Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What picture is used to help the reader imagine the earth’s testimony?
questions.answer: The earth is compared to a giant person speaking with one voice.

questions.question: What effect did this scene have on the traveler?
questions.answer: It gave him a clear understanding of the truth being shown.

questions.question: Besides birds, what other living creatures are included in this shared witness?
questions.answer: All species of animals are included.

questions.question: How do senses and inner abilities function in the passage?
questions.answer: They act like meaningful signs that show careful design.

questions.question: How do limbs, organs, and tools of the body function in the passage?
questions.answer: They serve as strong signs that point to wise and complete creation.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by linking creation with will?
questions.answer: That living things are not made randomly but by deliberate choice.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by linking decoration with purpose?
questions.answer: That beauty and distinction in creatures are meaningful, not useless.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by linking shaping with wisdom?
questions.answer: That each form is given in a measured and wise way.

questions.question: Why is it important that eggs and sperm are described as similar to one another?
questions.answer: It shows that very different creatures come from simple and closely alike starting points.

questions.question: What does the limited number of these beginnings emphasize?
questions.answer: It highlights how amazing it is that so many forms arise from such restricted sources.

questions.question: How are the forms of animals described after they develop?
questions.answer: They are orderly, different from one another, varied, and beyond counting.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is the passage using when it moves from similar beginnings to diverse creatures?
questions.answer: It is using evidence from creation to infer a wise and powerful Creator.

questions.question: If someone understood this passage well, what conclusion should they reach?
questions.answer: They should realize that the living world is a united sign of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do all animal species do together?
questions.answer: They join in bearing witness to the truth that Allah is one.

questions.question: Is this witness shown as scattered and separate, or united and shared? Explain.
questions.answer: It is shown as united and shared, because all species agree in the same testimony.

questions.question: What comparison helps explain the size and strength of this witness?
questions.answer: The whole earth is compared to one great human speaking.

questions.question: What did the traveler understand when he saw this?
questions.answer: He grasped the meaning of the animal world’s testimony with certainty.

questions.question: Which parts of animals are said to “speak” this witness?
questions.answer: Their senses, powers, limbs, members, and bodily instruments.

questions.question: Are these “words” actual speech with tongues, or signs through creation?
questions.answer: They are signs through creation and design.

questions.question: What three big ideas are connected with how animals are made?
questions.answer: Bringing into being, distinguishing and beautifying, and measuring and shaping.

questions.question: Which of these three is tied to will?
questions.answer: Bringing into existence and creating.

questions.question: Which of these three is tied to purpose?
questions.answer: Making creatures distinct and giving them beauty.

questions.question: Which of these three is tied to wisdom?
questions.answer: Giving proportion and form.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both order and variety in animal forms?
questions.answer: To show that creatures are not chaotic; they are both carefully arranged and richly diverse.

questions.question: What starting materials are named for the coming forth of animal life?
questions.answer: Eggs and drops of sperm.

questions.question: What is surprising about the relationship between these beginnings and the creatures that come from them?
questions.answer: Similar and limited beginnings produce many different and countless forms.

questions.question: What final belief is strengthened by all these signs together?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah’s necessary existence and absolute oneness.

questions.question: What statement of faith is supported by the animal world in this passage?
questions.answer: The statement that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does the agreement of all animals and birds show?
questions.answer: It shows a shared witness to Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: Why is the image of the earth as a great person meaningful here?
questions.answer: It helps us picture all living creatures giving one combined testimony.

questions.question: What direction does this testimony travel according to the passage?
questions.answer: It rises toward the dwellers of the heavens.

questions.question: What does the traveler’s reaction tell us about the strength of the evidence?
questions.answer: It was strong enough for him to understand it fully.

questions.question: What are some non-verbal ways animals are said to testify?
questions.answer: Through their abilities, body systems, organs, and balanced design.

questions.question: Why might the passage call these features “eloquent”?
questions.answer: Because they clearly communicate meaning even without spoken language.

questions.question: What does “bringing into being” tell us about living things?
questions.answer: That their existence comes from a Creator.

questions.question: What does “distinction and decoration” tell us about living things?
questions.answer: That each creature is given special qualities and beauty for a reason.

questions.question: What does “proportioning and forming” tell us about living things?
questions.answer: That their shapes and measurements are wisely arranged.

questions.question: How does the passage use cause and effect?
questions.answer: It shows that careful creation, meaningful beauty, and wise design lead us to recognize one Creator.

questions.question: Why mention that the animal forms are beyond counting?
questions.answer: To stress the vastness of Allah’s creative power.

questions.question: Why mention that eggs and sperm are limited in number?
questions.answer: To contrast their small, restricted beginnings with the huge variety produced from them.

questions.question: What idea is repeated by describing beginnings as alike and outcomes as different?
questions.answer: That amazing diversity comes from simple similar sources by Allah’s will.

questions.question: In one sentence, summarize the lesson of this passage.
questions.answer: The animal world, in all its design and variety, acts as a united proof of Allah’s oneness and wise creation.

questions.question: Who is giving testimony in this passage?
questions.answer: All species of animals, including birds, are giving testimony.

questions.question: What are they testifying to?
questions.answer: They are testifying to Allah’s existence and His being one.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this testimony is not weak or isolated?
questions.answer: It says the testimony comes from the agreement of all these creatures together.

questions.question: What image is used to show the earth speaking?
questions.answer: The earth is pictured as if it were one giant human being.

questions.question: What does this image teach about the natural world?
questions.answer: It teaches that creation as a whole points to Allah in a unified way.

questions.question: What kinds of “words” do animals have in the passage?
questions.answer: They have signs in their senses, powers, limbs, and body parts.

questions.question: Why are these signs important for understanding the message of the passage?
questions.answer: Because they show design, purpose, and order in living things.

questions.question: What part of the passage points to Allah’s will?
questions.answer: The part about bringing creatures into existence and creating them.

questions.question: What part points to purpose?
questions.answer: The part about making them distinct and beautified.

questions.question: What part points to wisdom?
questions.answer: The part about measuring and shaping them properly.

questions.question: How are the forms of animals described?
questions.answer: They are arranged, different, varied, and too many to fully count.

questions.question: What is the source of these many forms?
questions.answer: They come from similar eggs and similar drops of sperm.

questions.question: What lesson comes from many forms coming from similar beginnings?
questions.answer: It shows the work of a Creator who knows, wills, and designs each creature.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both similarity and difference?
questions.answer: It highlights the contrast between simple beginnings and diverse results.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful reader notice most in this passage?
questions.answer: That every part of the animal world can be read as a sign pointing to Allah.

questions.question: What united conclusion do the three truths produce in the passage?
questions.answer: They produce the conclusion that all animals together witness Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: How broad is this testimony according to the passage?
questions.answer: It includes the whole earth through all species of animals and birds.

questions.question: What does the comparison to a “great man” help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us imagine the earth as giving one mighty and meaningful testimony.

questions.question: What did the traveler gain from observing this scene?
questions.answer: He gained a complete understanding of what the testimony meant.

questions.question: What is special about the way animals and birds praise Allah here?
questions.answer: Their very creation and abilities act like praise and witness.

questions.question: Name two areas in animals that are presented as signs.
questions.answer: Their senses and their bodily organs.

questions.question: What do the descriptions of balance and order suggest about animal life?
questions.answer: They suggest that it is intentionally designed, not accidental.

questions.question: What does creation according to will tell us about Allah’s action?
questions.answer: It tells us that He creates by choice.

questions.question: What does distinction and adornment according to purpose tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us that differences and beauty in creatures have meaning and aim.

questions.question: What does shaping according to wisdom tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us that each form is made with understanding and perfect measure.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the number of animal forms?
questions.answer: It describes them as limitless in variety.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the starting points of those forms?
questions.answer: It describes them as similar and limited, such as eggs and sperm.

questions.question: Why is this contrast strong evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: Because countless well-formed creatures coming from similar small beginnings points to deliberate design.

questions.question: What kind of Creator is implied by this evidence?
questions.answer: A Creator who is one, powerful, willing, purposeful, and wise.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage for an 8th grader?
questions.answer: Animals and birds, through the way they are made, all point to Allah as the one true Creator.
